pr_title: Implement IUtf8SpanFormattable on all the numeric types in corelib
pr_body:
Augments SByte, Byte, Int16, UInt16, Int32, UInt32, Int64, UInt64, IntPtr, UIntPtr, Int128, UInt128, Half, Single, Double, NFloat, and Decimal to implement IUtf8SpanFormattable. Also fixes corelib TODOs around using IUtf8SpanFormattable. And removes some duplicate code from Utf8Formatter.

There is still more consolidation to be done between FormattingHelpers and Number.Formatting.

There are a few small (e.g. a few nanoseconds) regressions on my machine.  I'm seeing what can be done about them.  There are also some improvements.  Most things are neutral.

For Utf8Formatter, most of the APIs are now just delegating into the corresponding IUtf8SpanFormattable functionality, which means things that weren't previously supported (e.g. various format specifiers) now are.  I opted not to block them.  We can revisit that decision if desired.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/84527
Contributes to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/81500

The second commit here tries to address some of the regressions seen on some platforms in CI after the DateTime change went in.  I did it in this PR in order to then be able to measure the end-to-end, as this PR was also modifying some of those code paths.  Details on the changes made are in the second commit description.  After merging this, we'll want to rebase @tannergooding's parsing PR in order to unify the interfaces introduced; Tanner, I can do that if you'd prefer, or you're of course welcome to.

issue_context.title: Use primitive type IUtf8SpanFormattable implementations
issue_context.body: As part of implementing IUtf8SpanFormattable, multiple places that could use primitive type implementations of the interface are currently implemented in other ways.  Once {U}Int32 and friends implement the interface, these locations (which are tagged with this issue) should be updated.
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-runtime See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
As part of implementing IUtf8SpanFormattable, multiple places that could use primitive type implementations of the interface are currently implemented in other ways. Once {U}Int32 and friends implement the interface, these locations (which are tagged with this issue) should be updated.
Author: stephentoub
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Runtime`, `untriaged`, `needs-area-label`
Milestone: -

review_comments: ValueListBuilder is used in other assemblies as well.

I wonder if its worth caching the invariant versions as a fast path for serializers, deserializers, and the general common default case?

I'd likewise expect we could reuse the backing array in the majority case. Most of the time we'll have 1-2 UTF-16 characters becoming 1-4 UTF-8 characters...
Sorry, I'm not following. What are you suggesting caching that's not already being cached here?

Avoiding the call to `Encoding.UTF8GetBytes` entirely for the most common scenario, since that won't be constant foldable as its currently setup and would be needed per symbol.

It might not actually be beneficial in practice, just a scenario that came to mind.

> Avoiding the call to Encoding.UTF8GetBytes entirely for the most common scenario, since that won't be constant foldable as its currently setup and would be needed per symbol.

Oh, I see, you mean initializing the field so that we don't pay for the GetBytes on the first use, basically just hardcoding it to the UTF8-equivalent of the literal the UTF16 fields are initialized to?
Right. I imagine we could optimize both the default and invariant cases this way and that it might minimally help things
Yeah, that makes sense.  Let me see how hard it would be.

I'm going to defer for now.  There are several places these fields are set, and I'm not even sure if the initial const string values initializing the utf16 fields are ever actually used... they seem to get overwritten by the other code paths.  I agree there's probably some value in doing something like what you suggest, in particular to avoid duplicate byte[]s being created for different cultures that actually share a common value for some of these fields, but let's hold off on complicating things for now to reap those benefits.
This is going to box if it isn't inlined, having it public -or- having an internal version of the API would allow us to avoid the issue entirely.

Why would it box?
https://sharplab.io/#v2:EYLgxg9gTgpgtADwGwBYA0AXEBDAzgWwB8ABAJgEYBYAKGIAYACY8gOgCUBXAOwwEt8YLAMIR8AB14AbGFADKMgG68wMXAG4aNYgGYGuDFA5gMDWQxAMAkgDEIEGgG8aDFwwDaAWRgYAFhAAmluKSABRevgFBYpIA8mJ8EFy4LAByEJZckrxc2QDmAJQAus6uxChWthAsHiH5DA4MAL40zdQ02RgyAGbYKhV2jiUuZQw1+RrUrVqkDEKD1K5MuiMAqrgwIWa4dQC8AHwMISE2dvnb1bUTjUA

In the IL, sure, and maybe tier 0. But this should be fine in tier 1, no?

C# doesn't emit a constrained call here, because its just a standard instance method. It emits a `ldfld`, `box`, `ldarg...`, `callvirt instance...`

This requires the JIT to devirtualize things (and it may, but not all runtimes do this as well as others).
This might be a place where C# could emit a constrained call to help the JIT, but I guess that'd require some work on Roslyn and confirmation it doesn't violate any language rules....

I don't think it's worth complicating the implementation for. To my knowledge, the JIT has avoided the box here for a long time. If we for other reasons choose to make the methods public, that's fine, but I don't want to introduce backdoors to handle other code generators that may not handle things as well. The JIT does loads of optimizations we rely on without fallbacks.

> This might be a place where C# could emit a constrained call to help the JIT, but I guess that'd require some work on Roslyn and confirmation it doesn't violate any language rules....

I'll open an issue if there isn't one already.
Why are these all explicitly implemented... I thought we had them being publicly implemented where the existing types publicly exposed the same UTF-16 functionality?
Did we agree to that? I'm ok with it personally, but I don't remember it being discussed.

That was certainly the intent from the proposal. Having them be explicit just hides relatively "core" functionality and means they can't be a simple and better replacement for `Utf8Formatter`.

I don't see it explicitly called out in the proposal though, I just listed it as `Initial types that will implement the interface`.

If there are concerns, we can bubble it up first thing in API review tomorrow.

> If there are concerns, we can bubble it up first thing in API review tomorrow.

Let's do that, to cross the `i`s and dot the `t`s as it were.  We can follow-up to make them all public subsequent to this PR if that's the decision.
Might be nice to generalize this to `TryFormatBinaryInteger` and then we could possibly deduplicate some more logic (can definitely be done in a separate PR)
Should Roslyn recognize DoesNotReturns in this throw helper so you don't need the bogus goto after it?

Roslyn only uses `DoesNotReturn` as part of definite assignment analysis, such as to support nullable reference types.

It doesn't impact reachability for control flow purposes or what IL actually has to be emitted to keep the JIT happy.
